=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:15814-15827 | severity=critical | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The new G3 hook in the final-merge ruleset-blocked branch, `_pr_final_ci_wiring_behind_update "${final_pr}" "${pr_head_sha}" "${default_branch}" "${REVIEW_FINAL_CI_WORKFLOW:-ci.yml}" blocked_status || true`, turns a deliberately cleared "" back into `ci.yml`. It also adds helper side effects and gh reads on that path: it sets PR_FINAL_CI_WIRING_OUTCOME/REASON and reads workflow runs, compare, user and comments. This breaks the required check `orchestrate-poll (0)` (run 45348234958, shard 3, head 5d517bfde15ee23ab2e9256762f9f7cf6e7f0a15): `FAIL test_stall_merge_final_ci_workflow_is_captured_and_cleared_for_other_paths`.
  WHY: The test exists only on main (merge ref), is not on the inherited-failures list, and blocks merge; after merge the poller would dispatch ci.yml on a path main deliberately left with final CI off. Severity disagreement: BLOCKER from sonnet, gemini, openai and glm; MAJOR from minimax (who also raised a MAJOR naming/back-compat finding at line 15823). The highest is used. Suggested fix: `${REVIEW_FINAL_CI_WORKFLOW-ci.yml}`, and skip the hook when the variable is set but empty.
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:921, 2785 | severity=critical | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `_pr_sync_merge_blocked_guard` (line 921, `"${REVIEW_FINAL_CI_WORKFLOW:-ci.yml}"`) and `_pr_final_ci_wiring_behind_update` (line 2785, `local REVIEW_FINAL_CI_WORKFLOW="${REVIEW_FINAL_CI_WORKFLOW:-${wiring_wf}}"`) treat a set-but-empty REVIEW_FINAL_CI_WORKFLOW like an unset one. That bypasses the "empty (off)" setting documented at README.md:174, which callers set on purpose at pr_checks_lib.sh:4023 and review_merge_train.sh:2392/2408.
  WHY: A caller with final CI off (for example review_autofix.yml:141 exporting '' and reached from review_rb_judge.sh:2504) can still take the merge lease, update the branch, post the ai:merge-base-sync marker and dispatch ci.yml on the update head. Severity disagreement: MAJOR from sonnet, gemini, glm and minimax (naming lens); NIT from minimax (correctness lens, line 2785); BLOCKER from openai, whose finding combines this with the poller hook. The highest is used. Suggested fix: the no-colon `-` default, plus skipping when the variable is set but empty.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:10812 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: Syntax error in python heredoc block.
  WHY: Gemini says invalid python in an injected block would crash the poller. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 explicitly rejected this as a slop-scan parser artefact on code this PR does not touch (the PR's only hunk in this file is at lines 15814-15827).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "The check costs no extra API call per PR per tick in the common case. Compare blob SHAs from data the caller already has, or from one cached read of the base's workflow blob SHAs per cycle." (G4)
  expected_change_site: scripts/review_final_ci_sweep.sh and its call into scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh (_pr_ensure_final_ci)
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: The sweep calls _pr_ensure_final_ci with the head ref but no base ref or cached workflow data (review_final_ci_sweep.sh:340). The helper reads the PR for the base ref (pr_checks_lib.sh:1283-1285) and requests a head-to-base compare (pr_checks_lib.sh:2676-2678), plus GET user and paginated comments on the behind branch. No per-cycle base workflow blob SHA cache is used. Minimax notes the deferral: the sweep file is outside the files_touched grant, the cost is documented in the helper header and capped by FINAL_CI_SWEEP_MAX_PER_TICK, and the reason is in entry[8] of pr_all_comments_context.txt. Sonnet and glm treat it as an accepted residual.
- requirement: "The head's ci.yml (and any other workflow file the final CI calls)" must be checked for base-side changes the head lacks. (G1)
  expected_change_site: scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh, _pr_final_ci_wiring_behind_update
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The helper checks only .github/workflows/<workflow> (line 2644: `wiring_path=".github/workflows/${wiring_wf}"`) and does not inspect local reusable workflows called by that workflow. A custom REVIEW_FINAL_CI_WORKFLOW that calls a local reusable workflow would still run from the stale branch copy. test_ci_workflow_calls_no_local_reusable_workflow pins the default ci.yml. Sonnet and glm consider this satisfied for the shipped ci.yml.
- requirement: "When the branch cannot be updated (conflict, lease held by another PR, update refused), the pipeline does not dispatch the final CI on the stale workflow. It records one clear reason on the PR and in the log." (G2)
  expected_change_site: scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh, _pr_final_ci_wiring_behind_update refusal and check-only paths
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: When the comment read fails (wiring_seen_rc=2), the refused-update path only warns `comment=skipped reason=notes_unreadable` and does not post (pr_checks_lib.sh:2824-2829). The check-only no_update_path posts only when the note read succeeds and finds no prior note (pr_checks_lib.sh:2747-2756 / 2747-49). Minimax, sonnet and glm describe this as a deliberate trade-off that avoids one comment per tick.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:line 921, in the _pr_sync_merge_blocked_guard hook: `_pr_final_ci_wiring_behind_update "${guard_pr}" "${guard_head}" "${guard_base_ref}" "${REVIEW_FINAL_CI_WORKFLOW:-ci.yml}" blocked_status`. Also line 2785, in _pr_final_ci_wiring_behind_update: `local REVIEW_FINAL_CI_WORKFLOW="${REVIEW_FINAL_CI_WORKFLOW:-${wiring_wf}}"`. The poller hook at scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:15823 uses the same pattern. | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `:-` expansions turn an empty REVIEW_FINAL_CI_WORKFLOW, the documented "off" setting (README.md:174), into ci.yml, and line 2785 re-enables the final-CI dispatch inside the update chain. Other sites honour empty: 1216-1219, 2251, 1516. Callers clear it at pr_checks_lib.sh:4023 and review_merge_train.sh:2392 and 2408.
  WHY: review_autofix.yml:141 exports '' for consumers that have not opted in. A guard call from review_rb_judge.sh:2504 with `ci/final (missing)` as the only blocker takes the lease, PUTs update-branch, posts the marker and dispatches ci.yml. Fix: `${REVIEW_FINAL_CI_WORKFLOW-ci.yml}` / `${REVIEW_FINAL_CI_WORKFLOW-${wiring_wf}}`, and skip when the variable is set but empty.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:lines 15817-15824, the new G3 hook in the final-merge ruleset-blocked branch | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The required check `orchestrate-poll (0)` fails on head 5d517bfde15ee23ab2e9256762f9f7cf6e7f0a15 (run 45348234958, shard 3) with `FAIL test_stall_merge_final_ci_workflow_is_captured_and_cleared_for_other_paths`. The test comes from main via the merge ref. The hook's `:-ci.yml` defeats main's clearing on non-stall paths.
  WHY: The red required check blocks the merge, and after a merge ci.yml would be dispatched where main left final CI off. The exact assertion could not be confirmed; the reviewer advises rebasing on main and applying the `-` fix.
- HARDENING: scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh, _pr_sync_merge_blocked_guard hook (line 921), scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:15823, _pr_final_ci_wiring_behind_update line 2785. Use the no-colon defaults, and guard each hook with `[ "${REVIEW_FINAL_CI_WORKFLOW+set}" != "set" ] || [ -n "${REVIEW_FINAL_CI_WORKFLOW}" ]`. Estimated lines changed: 4. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3.
- NOTE: Task gaps: NONE. G4 sweep cost is deferred (sweep file outside the grant). G2 notes_unreadable is accepted. G1 is pinned by test_ci_workflow_calls_no_local_reusable_workflow. The last-run diff is a comment-only change above _pr_ensure_final_ci and is accurate. Gemini's orchestrate_poll_process.sh:10812 heredoc finding is dropped as a slop-scan artefact on untouched code.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

  WHY: With `ci/final (missing)` as the only blocker and a successful ci.yml run on the head, a caller with final CI disabled can update the PR branch and dispatch ci.yml.

  PROBLEM: The G3 hook uses ${REVIEW_FINAL_CI_WORKFLOW:-ci.yml}, which defaults to ci.yml when the variable is deliberately cleared (for example auto-merge off or e2e-smoke-test).
  WHY: The check-run orchestrate-poll (0) fails on test stall_merge_final_ci_workflow_is_captured_and_cleared_for_other_paths, breaking the merge pipeline.

  Evidence of absence: Only .github/workflows/<workflow> is checked; local reusable workflows a configurable REVIEW_FINAL_CI_WORKFLOW calls can run from a stale branch copy.

  Evidence of absence: When the comment read fails, the refusal path only warns (pr_checks_lib.sh:2824-2829). The check-only path posts only after a successful read with no prior note (pr_checks_lib.sh:2747-2756).

It sets PR_FINAL_CI_WIRING_OUTCOME/REASON, issues `GET actions/workflows/<wf>/runs?head_sha=<head>&per_page=20` (line 2649 of `scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh`), and may take the merge lease, update the branch, POST the marker and call _pr_base_sync_dispatch_final_ci. orchestrate-poll (0) shard 3 fails `test_stall_merge_final_ci_workflow_is_captured_and_cleared_for_other_paths` (run 45348234958, 44 passed / 1 failed).
